item.title: US jury finds 'Sandwich guy' not guilty of assaulting border agent with sub
item.description: A US protester, Sean Dunn, was found not guilty of assaulting a CBP agent with a sandwich. Prosecutors, under a Trump-ordered crackdown, sought felony charges, but a jury acquitted him of a misdemeanor. The defense argued the prosecution was an abuse of power, questioning if throwing a soft object constituted an offense.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: SNAP benefits: US federal judge orders Trump administration to release full payments amid shutdown
item.description: A US federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to fully fund SNAP benefits for millions of Americans. The ruling came after the administration proposed only covering 65% of the maximum benefit, potentially leaving recipients without food. The judge criticized the administration's failure to consider the severe consequences for those relying on the program.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Michael Burry, famous for ‘The Big Short,’ targets Nvidia and Palantir: What’s his net worth?
item.description: Michael Burry, famed for predicting the 2008 housing crash, has made a striking comeback, betting $1.1 billion against AI leaders Nvidia and Palantir through Scion Asset Management. With two-thirds of the fund concentrated on Palantir alone, Burry signals his conviction that AI valuations are dangerously inflated. Scion Asset Management now oversees roughly $1.38 billion in assets.

item.title: Asmongold urges advertisers and Amazon to act after Twitch unbans Nina Lin
item.description: Popular streamer Asmongold has strongly criticized Twitch's decision to unban creator Nina Lin after a short suspension. He argues this shows double standards in moderation. Asmongold is urging advertisers and Amazon leadership to intervene. This incident highlights ongoing concerns about Twitch's fairness and transparency in enforcing its rules for all creators.

item.title: 'The Big Short' Michael Burry bets $1 billion on Nvidia and Palantir's collapse: Is the AI boom heading for a crash?
item.description: Michael Burry, famous for predicting the 2008 financial crisis, is now betting $1.1 billion against AI giants Nvidia and Palantir, warning that the sector is in a bubble. Drawing comparisons to the dot-com and 2008 crashes, Burry’s contrarian stance and cryptic social media posts suggest AI valuations are dangerously overinflated and ripe for a sharp market correction.
item.dc:creator: TOI Business Desk

item.title: MrBeast gives fans a first glimpse of Beast Land his upcoming real life theme park
item.description: YouTuber MrBeast has unveiled Beast Land, a futuristic theme park inspired by his viral challenge videos. Opening November 13, 2025, in Saudi Arabia, the park features custom-built games like Tower Siege and Drop Zone, rollercoasters, and a massive prize wall. This ambitious project promises an immersive, competition-based experience, blending gaming and physical activity for an entirely new entertainment venture.

item.title: ‘Why would I talk now?’: Marco Rubio shuts down reporters in viral Capitol clip
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio's refusal to speak with reporters outside a classified briefing has sparked debate. Captured on video, Rubio stated, "I didn’t talk to you guys when I worked here. Why would I talk to you now?" Supporters hail his firm stance against the press, while critics deem it evasive, highlighting a shift in his media engagement style.

item.title: UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed announces 2026 as the Year of the Family
item.description: President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed has announced 2026 as the Year of the Family, reinforcing the UAE’s commitment to strong, stable households. Aligned with the National Family Growth Agenda 2031, the initiative promotes family cohesion, unity, and cultural values. It engages multiple sectors to support growth, wellbeing, and long-term national prosperity, recognising families as the cornerstone of Emirati society.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kash Patel's girlfriend sues Sam Parker for calling her a Jewish spy: 'She has never even been to Israel'
item.description: Country singer Alexis Wilkins, partner of FBI Director Kash Patel, is suing Sam Parker for $5 million after he falsely accused her of being an Israeli spy on social media. The lawsuit states Wilkins is a Christian, American-born citizen who has never been to Israel. Patel defended Wilkins, calling her a patriot and a rock-solid conservative.

item.title: 'Got a dupe LV?' think twice: Ajman Police and Louis Vuitton just teamed up to end the fake trade
item.description: Ajman Police has partnered with Louis Vuitton to combat counterfeit luxury goods, enhancing market patrols and officer training. This alliance follows a significant seizure of AED 30 million worth of fake items, reinforcing the UAE's commitment to robust intellectual property protection and consumer trust.

item.title: Nancy Pelosi announces retirement: The moment when she clapped at Trump after his call for 'unity' in Congress
item.description: Nancy Pelosi's impactful political career concludes, marked by legislative prowess and symbolic moments. Her iconic 2019 'Pelosi Clap' for Donald Trump, a gesture of restrained defiance, became a viral symbol of controlled opposition and the era's political mood. Beyond this memorable image, her legacy includes landmark legislation and leadership through crises, solidifying her influence.

item.title: 'She was evil, corrupt': Trump reacts to Nancy Pelosi's announcement of retirement; 'I'm honored...'
item.description: Nancy Pelosi announced her retirement from Congress, ending a decades-long career. President Donald Trump reacted by calling her "evil, corrupt" and "highly overrated," while also referencing her two impeachment attempts against him. Pelosi, the first and only female Speaker of the House, expressed her love for serving San Francisco and her commitment to democracy.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 43-year-old Illinois woman charged after allegedly conceiving child with her daughter’s 14-year-old dance date
item.description: A 43-year-old Illinois woman, Robyn Polston, faces serious charges including criminal sexual assault. She allegedly conceived a child with a 14-year-old boy who attended a junior high dance as her daughter's date. Investigators uncovered digital evidence and DNA confirmed the boy as the father. Polston was arrested and is held without bail.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nikki Haley's son calls Vivek Ramaswamy's lessons from Zohran Mamdani's winning cringe
item.description: Following election defeats, Vivek Ramaswamy urged Republicans to focus on affordability and abandon identity politics. However, Nalin Haley, son of Nikki Haley, countered, arguing the GOP should embrace religious identity, calling Ramaswamy's views outdated and cringe.

item.title: Saudi Arabia grants premium residency to 100+ global entrepreneurs from over 20 nationalities
item.description: Saudi Arabia has granted Premium Residency to more than 100 entrepreneurs representing over 20 nationalities, reinforcing its goal of becoming a global hub for innovation and investment. Announced at the Biban Forum 2025 in Riyadh, the initiative supports start-ups, drives economic growth, and aligns with Saudi Vision 2030’s focus on attracting global talent and fostering entrepreneurship.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pakistan breaches truce again: Islamabad fires into Afghanistan amid peace talks, say reports
item.description: Pakistan has reportedly violated the ceasefire by firing into Afghanistan, even as officials meet in Istanbul for renewed talks with Taliban representatives. This comes after a previous agreement for a ceasefire and a monitoring mechanism, following deadly border clashes. The ongoing discussions aim to de-escalate tensions between the neighbours.
